facts.claim: A resident taxpayer is eligible to claim credit for any foreign tax paid in a country or specified territory outside India.
facts.subject: resident_taxpayer
facts.evidence: As per Rule 128 of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, a resident taxpayer is eligible to claim credit for any foreign tax paid, in a country or specified territory outside India.

facts.claim: Form 67 must be submitted through online mode.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: Form 67 can only be submitted through online mode.

facts.claim: A registered user on the e-Filing portal with a valid user ID and password is required to use this service.
facts.subject: form_67_service
facts.evidence: • Registered user on the e-Filing portal with valid user ID and password.

facts.claim: The PAN and Aadhaar of the taxpayer must be linked to use this service (recommended).
facts.subject: form_67_service
facts.evidence: • PAN and Aadhaar of the taxpayer are linked. (Recommended)

facts.claim: The PAN of the taxpayer must be active to use this service.
facts.subject: form_67_service
facts.evidence: • Status of PAN of Taxpayer should be "Active"

facts.claim: Form 67 is required to be submitted on or before the due date specified for furnishing the return of income under sub-section (1) of Section 139.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: A resident taxpayer who has credit for the amount of any foreign tax paid in a country outside India by way of deduction or otherwise will be required to furnish the statement in Form 67 on or before the due date specified for furnishing the return of income under sub-section (1) of Section 139 to claim credit of such taxes.

facts.claim: Form 67 is also required to be submitted in case the carry backward of loss of the current year results in a refund of foreign tax for which credit has been claimed in any earlier previous years.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: Form 67 will also be required to be furnished in case the carry backward of loss of the current year results in refund of foreign tax for which credit has been claimed in any earlier previous years.

facts.claim: Form 67 has four sections: Part A, Part B, Verification, and Attachments.
facts.subject: form_67

detail.sections: Part A, Part B, Verification, Attachments

facts.evidence:
Form 67 has 4 sections:
Part A
Part B
Verification
Attachments

facts.claim: Part A of Form 67 requires basic information such as name, PAN or Aadhaar, address, and assessment year.
facts.subject: form_67_part_a

detail.information: name, PAN or Aadhaar, address, assessment year

facts.evidence: Part A of the form entails basic information such as your Name, PAN or Aadhaar, Address and Assessment Year.

facts.claim: Part A of Form 67 requires the addition of receipt details of income from a country or specified territory outside India and the foreign tax credit claimed.
facts.subject: form_67_part_a

detail.details: receipt details of income from a country or specified territory outside India and foreign tax credit claimed

facts.evidence: You are also required to the add the receipt details of the income from a country or specified territory outside India and Foreign Tax Credit claimed.

facts.claim: Part B of Form 67 requires details of refund of foreign tax as a result of carry backward of losses and disputed foreign tax.
facts.subject: form_67_part_b

detail.details: refund of foreign tax as a result of carry backward of losses and disputed foreign tax

facts.evidence: Part B of the form is where you will be required to provide details of refund of foreign tax as result of carry backward of losses and disputed foreign tax.

facts.claim: The Verification section of Form 67 contains a self-declaration form as per Rule 128 of the Income Tax Rules, 1962.
facts.subject: form_67_verification

detail.rule: Rule 128 of the Income Tax Rules, 1962

facts.evidence: The Verification section contains a self-declaration form containing fields as per Rule 128 of the Income Tax Rules, 1962.

facts.claim: The Attachments section of Form 67 requires a copy of the certificate or statement and proof of payment or deduction of foreign tax.
facts.subject: form_67_attachments

detail.attachments: copy of the certificate or statement and proof of payment / deduction of foreign tax

facts.evidence: The last section of Form 67 is Attachments where you need to attach a copy of the certificate or statement and proof of payment / deduction of foreign tax.

facts.claim: Form 67 can be accessed and submitted only through the e-Filing portal in online mode.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: You can fill and submit Form 67 only in online mode through the e-Filing portal.

facts.claim: To submit Form 67, a user must log in to the e-Filing portal using their user ID and password.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: Step 1: Log in to the e-Filing portal using your user ID and password.

facts.claim: If the PAN is not linked with Aadhaar, a pop-up message will appear indicating that the PAN is made inoperative.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: For Individual users, if PAN is not linked with the Aadhaar you will see a pop-up message that your PAN is made inoperative as it is not linked with your Aadhaar.

facts.claim: To submit Form 67, a user must navigate to the e-File > Income Tax Forms > File Income Tax Forms section on the Dashboard.
facts.subject: form_67_submission

detail.path: e-File > Income Tax Forms > File Income Tax Forms

facts.evidence: Step 2: On your Dashboard, click e-File > Income Tax Forms > File Income Tax Forms.

facts.claim: To submit Form 67, a user must select the Assessment Year (A.Y.) and click Continue.
facts.subject: form_67_submission

detail.action: select Assessment Year and click Continue

facts.evidence: Step 4 : On the Form 67 page, select the Assessment Year (A.Y.) and click Continue.

facts.claim: After filling Form 67, a user must click Preview to verify the details.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: Step 6 : On click of Let's Get Started , Form 67 is displayed. Fill all the required details and click Preview .

facts.claim: After previewing Form 67, a user must click Proceed to e-Verify.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: Step 7: On the Preview page, verify the details and click Proceed to e-Verify.

facts.claim: A user must e-Verify Form 67 to complete the submission.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: Step 8 : Click Yes to e-Verify..

facts.claim: After successful e-Verification, a Transaction ID and Acknowledgement Number are provided for future reference.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: After successful e-Verification, a success message is displayed along with a Transaction ID and Acknowledgement Number. Please keep a note of the Transaction ID and Acknowledgement for future reference.

facts.claim: A confirmation message is sent to the email ID registered on the e-Filing portal after Form 67 submission.
facts.subject: form_67_submission
facts.evidence: You will also receive a confirmation message on the email ID registered on the e-Filing portal.

facts.claim: Applicants must attach a copy of the certificate or statement and proof of payment or deduction of foreign tax.
facts.subject: form_67
facts.evidence: The last section of Form 67 is Attachments where you need to attach a copy of the certificate or statement and proof of payment / deduction of foreign tax.

facts.claim: A taxpayer must be a registered PAN user on the e-Filing portal to request a challan correction.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence:
Pre-requisites
|
Registered PAN user on the e-Filing portal

facts.claim: Challan correction requests can only be submitted after logging into the e-Filing portal.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Challan correction request can only be submitted post-login (after logging into e-Filing portal) facility.

facts.claim: The challan to be corrected should not have been consumed during processing.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Challan to be corrected should not be consumed during processing

facts.claim: Challan correction requests should not be pending with any other authority.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Challan correction request should not be pending with any other authority

facts.claim: Challans pertaining to Assessment Year 2020-21 onwards are available for correction through the e-filing portal.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: The Challans pertaining to A.Y 2020-21 onwards are available for correction currently through the e-filing portal.

facts.claim: Challan correction requests can be made only once on the e-filing portal for any submitted challan.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Challan Correction request will be allowed only once on the e-filing portal for any submitted challan.

facts.claim: The time window for correction requests for changing Major Head (Tax Applicable) and Minor Head (Type of payment) is within 30 days of the Challan Deposit Date.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: The time window for the correction request by taxpayer for changing Major Head (Tax Applicable) and Minor Head (Type of payment) on the e-filing portal will be within 30 days of the Challan Deposit Date

facts.claim: The time window for correction requests for changing AY/Tax year is within 7 days of the Challan Deposit Date.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: The time window for the correction request by taxpayer for changing AY/Tax year on the e-filing portal will be within 7 days of the Challan Deposit Date.

facts.claim: Challan correction requests can be submitted for Minor Heads 100 (Advance Tax), 300 (Self-Assessment Tax), and 400 (Demand Payment as Regular Assessment Tax).
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Challan Correction Request can be submitted only for Minor Heads 100 (Advance Tax), 300 (Self-Assessment Tax) 400 (Demand Payment as Regular Assessment Tax)

facts.claim: Challan correction requests for Minor Heads other than 100, 300, and 400 must be submitted to the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Please submit challan correction request to Jurisdictional Assessing Officer for Minor Heads other than 100, 300 and 400

facts.claim: Challan correction requests must be e-verified using Aadhaar OTP, DSC, EVC, or other options.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: You are now required to e-Verify the challan correction request either through Aadhaar OTP, DSC, EVC or other options.

facts.claim: It may take 7–20 days for the challan correction status to be updated on the portal.
facts.subject: challan_correction_status
facts.evidence: Note: It may take 7–20 days for the challan correction status to be updated on the portal.

facts.claim: An applicant can check the status of a challan correction request by clicking 'View Challan Correction Status' after e-verification.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Step 9: Post e-verification, a success message will be displayed. You can click View Challan Correction Status to know the status of challan correction.

facts.claim: To check the status of a challan correction request, an applicant can repeat steps 1 to 3 and view details on the challan correction page.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Step 10: To Check Challan Correction Request Status, please repeat Step 1 to Step 3 . At challan correction page” You can view details and check status for Challan Correction Requests raised by you”.

facts.claim: Log in to the e-Filing portal with user ID and password.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Step 1: Log in to the e-Filing portal with user ID and password.

facts.claim: On the Dashboard, click Services > Challan Correction.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Step 2: On the Dashboard, click Services > Challan Correction.

facts.claim: On the Challan Correction page, click the “+ Create Challan Correction Request” option to create a new Challan Correction Request.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Step 3: On the Challan Correction page, click the “+ Create Challan Correction Request” option to create a new Challan Correction Request.

facts.claim: You are required to select the relevant attribute for correction in the challan. Select the appropriate option (multiple options can be selected as applicable)and click Continue.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Step 4: You are required to select the relevant attribute for correction in the challan. Select the appropriate option (multiple options can be selected as applicable)and click Continue.

facts.claim: You are required to select the Tax year/Assessment Year or Challan Identification Number (CIN) to create challan correction request .Based on selection the unconsumed challans will be displayed for the correction. Click Continue to proceed.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Step 5: You are required to select the Tax year/Assessment Year or Challan Identification Number (CIN) to create challan correction request .Based on selection the unconsumed challans will be displayed for the correction. Click Continue to proceed.

facts.claim: Once the relevant challan is selected, the Correction in Challan page will open. On this page, the user can update the required challan attributes and then click Continue.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Step 6: Once the relevant challan is selected, the Correction in Challan page will open. On this page, the user can update the required challan attributes and then click Continue.

facts.claim: Users may raise a grievance on the e Filing portal if their correction request status shows 'Pending' for a long time.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence:
Users can check the status under Services → Challan Correction.
If the status remains pending beyond reasonable timelines, users may:
• Raise a grievance on the e Filing portal, or
• Contact their Jurisdictional Assessing Officer.

facts.claim: An applicant can check the status of a challan correction request under 'Services → Challan Correction' on the e-Filing portal.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Users can check the status under Services → Challan Correction.

facts.claim: Applicants receive email and SMS notifications once the challan correction is processed.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request
facts.evidence: Yes. Users receive email and SMS notifications on their registered email ID and mobile number once the challan correction request is processed.

facts.claim: The applicant can download the corrected challan details after the correction has been processed.
facts.subject: challan_correction_request

detail.path: Post Login → Services → Challan Correction → Download Corrected Details

facts.evidence: You can download the corrected challan details using the following path: Path: Post Login → Services → Challan Correction → Download Corrected Details

facts.claim: A taxpayer must e-verify their return before refund processing can start.
facts.subject: refund_processing
facts.evidence: Refund processing by the tax department starts only after the return is e-verified by the taxpayer.

facts.claim: A taxpayer must have a valid User ID and Password to check refund status.
facts.subject: refund_status_check
facts.evidence: Valid User ID and Password

facts.claim: A taxpayer must have their PAN linked with their Aadhaar number to check refund status.
facts.subject: refund_status_check
facts.evidence: PAN is linked with Aadhaar number

facts.claim: A taxpayer must have filed an ITR claiming a refund to check refund status.
facts.subject: refund_status_check
facts.evidence: ITR filed claiming refund

facts.claim: A taxpayer must check their refund status on the e-filing portal.
facts.subject: refund_status_check
facts.evidence: The taxpayer can also check refund status on the e-filing as per the process detailed hereunder.

facts.claim: A taxpayer must ensure their bank account is pre-validated to avoid refund failure.
facts.subject: refund_success
facts.evidence: 1. In case the bank account is not pre-validated. It is now compulsory to pre-validate your bank account.

facts.claim: A taxpayer must ensure the name on their bank account matches their PAN card details to avoid refund failure.
facts.subject: refund_success
facts.evidence: 2. The name mentioned in the bank account does not match with PAN card details.

facts.claim: A taxpayer must ensure the IFSC code provided is valid to avoid refund failure.
facts.subject: refund_success
facts.evidence: 3. In case of an invalid IFSC code.

facts.claim: A taxpayer must ensure the bank account mentioned in the ITR is not closed to avoid refund failure.
facts.subject: refund_success
facts.evidence: 4. If the account that you have mentioned in the ITR has been closed.

facts.claim: A taxpayer must check for intimation regarding discrepancies in ITR if the refund is not received within 4-5 weeks.
facts.subject: refund_check
facts.evidence: However, if refund is not received during this duration, the taxpayer must check for intimation regarding discrepancies in ITR; check email for any notification from the IT department regarding the refund.

facts.claim: A taxpayer must check the refund status for the desired Assessment year on the e-filing portal.
facts.subject: refund_status_check
facts.evidence: Step 4: Now you can check the refund status for the desired Assessment year.

facts.claim: The 'Know Your JAO' service is available to taxpayers who have a valid PAN.
facts.subject: know_your_jao_service
facts.evidence: The ‘Know Your JAO’ service is available to taxpayers who have a valid PAN.

facts.claim: The 'Know Your JAO' service is available to both registered or unregistered users on the e-Filing portal.
facts.subject: know_your_jao_service
facts.evidence: This service is available to both registered or unregistered user on e-Filing portal.

facts.claim: A valid mobile number is a prerequisite for availing the 'Know Your JAO' service.
facts.subject: know_your_jao_service
facts.evidence: Valid mobile number

facts.claim: To use the 'Know Your JAO' service, a taxpayer must enter their PAN and a valid mobile number on the e-Filing portal.
facts.subject: know_your_jao_service
facts.evidence: On the ‘ Know Your Jurisdictional Assessing Officer’ page, enter your PAN and a valid mobile number and click ‘Continue’ .

facts.claim: A 6-digit OTP will be sent to the mobile number entered for the 'Know Your JAO' service.
facts.subject: know_your_jao_service
facts.evidence: You will receive a 6-digit OTP on the mobile number you entered in Step 2.

facts.claim: The OTP for the 'Know Your JAO' service is valid for 15 minutes.
facts.subject: otp
facts.evidence: OTP will be valid for 15 minutes only.

facts.claim: A taxpayer has 3 attempts to enter the correct OTP for the 'Know Your JAO' service.
facts.subject: otp
facts.evidence: You have 3 attempts to enter the correct OTP.

facts.claim: A new OTP can be generated by clicking 'Resend OTP' for the 'Know Your JAO' service.
facts.subject: otp
facts.evidence: On clicking ‘Resend OTP’, a new OTP will be generated and sent.

facts.claim: On successful OTP validation, the taxpayer will see the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer Details for the 'Know Your JAO' service.
facts.subject: otp
facts.evidence: On successful OTP validation, you will see the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer Details (such as Area Code, AO Type, Range Code, AO Number, Jurisdiction, Address and email ID of the JAO), along with status of your PAN.

facts.claim: Go to the e-Filing portal homepage. In quick links section, click ‘ Know Your JAO’ .
facts.subject: know_your_jao
facts.evidence: Step 1: Go to the e-Filing portal homepage. In quick links section, click ‘ Know Your JAO’ .

facts.claim: On the ‘ Know Your Jurisdictional Assessing Officer’ page, enter your PAN and a valid mobile number and click ‘Continue’ .
facts.subject: know_your_jao
facts.evidence: Step 2 : On the ‘ Know Your Jurisdictional Assessing Officer’ page, enter your PAN and a valid mobile number and click ‘Continue’ .

facts.claim: You will receive a 6-digit OTP on the mobile number you entered in Step 2. Enter the OTP and click ‘ Validate ’.
